descriptor: Live event promotion, venue operation & ticketing (Ticketmaster) · reported in USD

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Segment Adjusted Operating Income (AOI)
charts.annotation: Concerts is ~83% of revenue but the thinnest promoter margin; Ticketing and Sponsorship are smaller but carry most of the profit.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue mix
segmentRevenue.content:
Live Nation reports three segments: Concerts (promotion, venue operation, concessions/parking/premium), Ticketing (Ticketmaster's per-ticket fees under 3-5 year client agreements) and Sponsorship & Advertising (brand deals monetising the fan base the other two segments aggregate).

For Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.: Concerts is ~83% of revenue, Ticketing ~12% and Sponsorship ~5% (FY2025) -- the mix is overwhelmingly show-by-show promotion, not the recurring ticketing fee stream investors often assume dominates.

What to watch:

  • Concerts growth driven by show count/scale versus ticket pricing
  • Whether Ticketing and Sponsorship grow faster than Concerts (margin mix shift)

segmentAOI.title: Segment Adjusted Operating Income (AOI)
segmentAOI.content:
AOI is Live Nation's non-GAAP operating profit measure by segment -- operating income before depreciation/amortisation and other non-cash/non-recurring items.

For Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.: the profit pool inverts the revenue mix -- Concerts promoter margins are thin (low single digits on show economics), while Ticketing and Sponsorship & Advertising run far higher margins on a fraction of the revenue. A good quarter for Concerts revenue is not automatically a good quarter for consolidated AOI.

What to watch:

  • Ticketing/Sponsorship AOI growing faster than their revenue (operating leverage)
  • Concerts AOI margin -- venue-operator revenue (concessions, parking, premium seating) is the lever management points to for expanding it

concertEvents.title: Concert events & attendance
concertEvents.content:
Concert events is the number of shows Live Nation promoted or hosted in the period; fans is total attendance across them, split North America/International.

For Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.: this is the physical-scale driver behind Concerts revenue -- more shows and bigger crowds, not higher prices, is how the segment has grown. International venues (127 of 460) are a minority of the footprint but the larger share of the growth narrative management gives.

What to watch:

  • Fans-per-event trend (bigger shows/venues vs more, smaller ones)
  • North America vs International growth rates

ticketingVolume.title: Ticketmaster ticket volume
ticketingVolume.content:
Fee-bearing tickets are the primary-market tickets Ticketmaster earns a per-ticket fee on; non-fee-bearing tickets (venue box office, some presales) pass through without that fee.

For Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.: fee-bearing volume, not total volume, is what moves Ticketing revenue and AOI -- a quarter with flat total tickets but a rising fee-bearing share is a better quarter for this segment than the headline count suggests.

What to watch:

  • Fee-bearing share of total tickets sold (mix, not just volume)
  • Ticketing revenue growth versus fee-bearing ticket growth (yield/fee-rate change)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
